record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Classify, up to polynomial automorphisms of C^2 on the source and affine automorphisms of C on the target, all primitive polynomials p(x,y) in two complex variables that have a fiber isomorphic to C*. Equivalently, determine a complete list of non-equivalent such polynomials so that every primitive polynomial with a C*-fiber is equivalent to one on the list.

evidence.quote:
PROBLEM. Find the list of non-equivalent polynomials such that every primitive
polynomial p with a C∗
-fiber is equivalent to one of polynomials from this list.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}^*=\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$. A polynomial $p\in\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ is called primitive if the generic fiber of the morphism $p:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is irreducible (equivalently, $p$ is not of the form $h\circ q$ for some $q\in\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ and some polynomial $h\in\mathbb{C}[t]$ of degree $\geq 2$). Say that $p$ has a $\mathbb{C}^*$-fiber if there exists $c\in\mathbb{C}$ such that the scheme-theoretic fiber $p^{-1}(c)\subset\mathbb{C}^2$, with its reduced structure, is isomorphic as an algebraic variety to $\mathbb{C}^*$.

Two primitive polynomials $p_1,p_2\in\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ are called equivalent if there exist a polynomial automorphism $\Phi\in\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{C}^2)$ and an affine automorphism $\psi(t)=at+b$ of $\mathbb{C}$ (with $a\in\mathbb{C}^*$, $b\in\mathbb{C}$) such that $p_2=\psi\circ p_1\circ\Phi$.

Problem. Produce an explicit list $\mathcal{L}\subset\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ of pairwise non-equivalent primitive polynomials such that every primitive polynomial $p\in\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ admitting a fiber isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^*$ is equivalent to exactly one polynomial in $\mathcal{L}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a definitive complete classification of primitive polynomials in two complex variables having a $\mathbb{C}^*$-fiber up to the stated equivalence. Related results exist (e.g., Kaliman's work on polynomials with general $\mathbb{C}^2$-fibers, and classifications of rational polynomials of simple type by Miyanishi–Sugie and corrections), but a full closed list addressing exactly this problem could not be verified from accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: Polynomials with general C^2-fibers are variables. I
status_evidence.snippet: Kaliman's work on polynomials with general fibers of a prescribed type, related to the broader program of classifying polynomial fibrations.
status_evidence.claim: Related classification results exist for polynomials with prescribed generic fiber, but the specific C*-fiber classification problem is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing cycles and monodromy of complex polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses primitive polynomials f:C^2 -> C and rational polynomials of simple type after Miyanishi-Sugie.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent classification work exists but does not provide a complete list for primitive polynomials with a C*-fiber.
